scope: Official NVIDIA documentation and interpretation for the cc12.0 texture/global K1 kernels. Architectural documentation is distinct from measured implementation evidence.

sources.title: CUDA Programming Guide: Compute Capabilities, shared-memory capacity table
claims: Compute capability 12.x has 128 KiB unified data-cache capacity per SM.
Supported shared-memory carveouts are 0, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 100 KiB.
The table gives a 28-128 KiB texture-cache working-set range, depending on configuration. The unified maximum is not a promise of private texture capacity.

sources.title: CUDA Programming Guide: Configuring L1/Shared Memory Balance
claims: cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout supports cudaSharedmemCarveoutMaxL1.
The attribute is a driver hint; the driver can choose a different carveout to execute the kernel.
An accepted preference or a queried preferred attribute does not establish the realized hardware partition; record profiler launch__shared_mem_config_size separately.
sources.interpretation: The final claim is an evidence distinction derived from preference semantics, rather than a cache-capacity guarantee.

sources.title: PTX ISA: Cache Operators, Cache Eviction Priority Hints and Memory Hierarchy
claims: Cache operators and eviction priorities are performance hints, not guaranteed cache pinning.
Global data is coherent at L2; separate L1 caches are not coherent for global data. The driver must invalidate global L1 lines between dependent grids.
Texture reads are not coherent with global or surface writes in the same kernel; safe texture updates precede the reading launch.
Persistence of the texture memory state space across launches means allocation/content lifetime, not guaranteed retention of its cache lines.
sources.interpretation: The last statement distinguishes persistent memory storage from cache residency. The global-L1 invalidation requirement alone does not prove exactly which texture lines Blackwell invalidated in a particular measurement.

sources.title: Nsight Compute Profiling Guide: Cache Control and L1/TEX Memory Tables
claims: Nsight Compute normally flushes caches before replay passes; application replay with cache-control none permits application priming but does not force retention.
L1 sectors are 32 bytes. Sector hit rate counts requested sectors that do not miss; it is not a snapshot of resident dictionary contents.
A texture instruction can produce multiple requests; request count is not necessarily executed instruction count.
L1 data, texture and shared data use the same physical resource. Texture data arriving through TEX and global/local data arriving through LSU can compete.
Query metric availability for the installed tool and target architecture; unavailable metrics must not become numerical zero.

sources.title: CUDA Binary Utilities: cuobjdump and nvdisasm
claims: cuobjdump can extract and disassemble cubins embedded in host executables; nvdisasm accepts cubins and offers richer analysis.
Preserve native sm_120 SASS and resource usage from the actual tested binary. TLD/TEX instructions substantiate the texture instruction path; they do not prove runtime residency.

sources.title: CUDA Programming Guide: Programming Model
claims: Thread blocks are scheduled among available SMs, with no guarantee about their assignment order.
A warm-up launch therefore does not guarantee that the next launch's corresponding block executes on the same SM or finds the same per-SM cache state.
sources.interpretation: The second statement follows from the absence of a block-to-SM assignment guarantee.

sources.title: CUDA C++ Programming Guide: Device Memory L2 Access Management
claims: L2 access-policy windows and persisting set-asides control preferential retention in L2, subject to supported sizes and competing use.
L2 persistence does not provide L1/texture cache pinning. The access-policy hitRatio field is a policy parameter, not a measured hit rate.

sources.title: CUDA Best Practices Guide: Texture Memory
claims: Texture fetches benefit from spatial locality. NVIDIA describes the texture path as streaming with constant fetch latency: cache hits reduce DRAM demand rather than fetch latency.
Texture fetching can be useful in some access patterns; native texture use alone does not establish superiority to coalesced global loads.

sources.title: NVIDIA Development Tools: ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM Nsight Compute
claims: ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM means the user lacks access to GPU performance counters.
The documented remedies involve administrative execution or enabling counter access. This project records restricted profiling honestly without silently changing privileges or system policy.
sources.interpretation: The final sentence applies the project operational contract, not an NVIDIA requirement.

sources.title: CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.8: Using TMA to transfer data
claims: Bulk asynchronous copies support one-dimensional global/shared transfers on supported architectures.
Global and shared pointers and transfer sizes require the documented alignment; a shared completion barrier and async-proxy ordering are part of correctness.
The implementation uses shared staging plus native bulk copies. Its cache effect is measured separately, not inferred from the instruction name.

sources.title: PTX ISA 8.7: cp.async.bulk and async-proxy memory ordering
claims: cp.async.bulk.shared::cta.global uses mbarrier complete-tx bytes for completion.
cp.async.bulk.global.shared::cta uses bulk async groups; the implementation commits and waits for complete group writes before shared storage reuse.
fence.proxy.async.shared::cta orders generic shared accesses with the async proxy. Cache residency is not a formal property proved by these ordering rules.

architecture_interpretation.capacity: 128 KiB is the cc12.x combined per-SM maximum. Subtract a realized 32 KiB shared-memory configuration to obtain a nominal 96 KiB remaining unified-cache capacity; this arithmetic is not a measurement of exclusively usable texture bytes.
architecture_interpretation.residency_boundary: No supported L1/texture pinning guarantee is established by these interfaces. Neither fitting within capacity nor disabling the profiler's own flushing promises retention across kernel launches.
architecture_interpretation.invalidation_boundary: The formal PTX documentation establishes dependent-grid global-L1 invalidation and texture coherence boundaries. The available measurement does not isolate whether texture-line invalidation, block scheduling, interference or other cache behavior caused its misses. Do not assert a specific Blackwell invalidation mechanism from this one sample.

review_measurement.format_note: CSV includes profiler preamble and a units row. Locale uses a dot as a thousands separator and a comma for fractional values. Values below are normalized from the measured kernel row.
review_measurement.inference: 2048 sectors times 32 bytes equals the entire 65536-byte packed dictionary. For this aligned one-pass read of the complete dictionary, total sector traffic matches the minimum unique-sector footprint. This is useful streaming efficiency despite 0% observed sector hits; it is not complete cache residency.
review_measurement.request_interpretation: 4096 threads form 128 warps; 256 texture requests are compatible with multiple TEX requests per warp instruction. Do not equate requests with fetch instructions.
review_measurement.optimization_objective: Preserve exact output semantics and minimize verified execution time, unnecessary fetch instructions, requested sectors and misses. A higher hit percentage produced by redundant rereads or fragmented accesses can accompany more work and worse performance. Report numerator and denominator, not hit percentage alone.

continuation_findings.instruction_cache: The Nsight architecture guide identifies instruction/constant caches separately from L1TEX; a large instruction footprint alone does not establish direct texture-data eviction.
continuation_findings.cg_boundary: L2-only cache requests do not establish zero activity in L1TEX data banks or promise that unrelated texture lines remain resident.
continuation_findings.control_boundary: A successful warm/reread control and a failing full epoch isolate additional workload effects. They do not by themselves identify allocation, invalidation, contention, preemption or cache replacement as the hardware cause.
continuation_findings.cache_priorities: PTX L1 eviction and no-allocation qualifiers are performance hints. A successful compile or accepted hint must be distinguished from measured residency.
